scope_findings: All27 noun systems give four cases in both numbers except the explicitly singular four-cell title Hǣlend. Gender and ending labels are correct.

All18 selected positive adjective systems have24 NGDA cells plus the two scoped masculine/neuter singular instrumental references; the comparative systems have24 NGDA cells and only as-dative instrumental pointers.

All7 finite verbal systems explicitly mean present/preterite indicative, with all persons and numbers. The ten participle cells are bases, the two gewītan cells commands, and the scēawian pair plain/inflected infinitives; scēawianne remains recognition.

The actual340 nonliteral nominal cells are recoverable through printed models and explicit lexical stems, including the mildheortnes and ceaster full-headword exceptions and the reduced comparative genitive.
The extra four-cell Hǣlend table correctly repeats its weall singular route and supplies no title plural. Title/name apposition is explicit.
Mass/abstract/fire/metal plural forms and astronomical plurals retain reference limits. Earlier Bearn identity and masculine sǣ are explicitly preserved.

Seolh h-loss plus lengthening, sumer retention, winter/frōfor/ceaster/seolfor syncope, īsern retention, bæð/geat/sīðfæt plural alternation, mildheortnes doubling and stille reduction all have actual learner rules supported by primary evidence.

Geatum, sumera/wintra, rēn, seol, disyllabic adjective variants and genēalǣhte receive bounded alternative notes; scōd and a separate strong bringan preterite are distinguished from the selected series.

findings.evidence: Cook p279 sends blæc to §57.2. Cook pp38–39 §57 prints glædra and states the æ/a alternation follows that paradigm. Cook p41 §60 selects weak genitive -ra. Wright p209/PDF229 §425 explicitly includes blæc among the short stems declined like glæd. Wright p217/PDF237 §440 identifies weak genitive -ra as the strong ending (§424), whose p207/PDF227 model is glædra. No checked source establishes a lexical weak blacra exception. Unit3 already teaches weak glædra before -ra; the actual cumulative register contains all three reviewed weak glædra genitive plurals.

diagnostic_reviews.actual_paragraph: **bæð**, bath (neuter). Stem **bæð-**. Genitive singular **bæðes**; dative singular **bæðe**; nominative plural **baðu**.

**męregrēote**, pearl (feminine). Stem **męregrēot-**. Genitive singular **męregrēotan**; dative singular **męregrēotan**; nominative plural **męregrēotan**. The weak feminine has nominative singular -e, the other singular cases -an, plural nominative and accusative -an, genitive -ena and dative -um.
**īgland**, island (neuter). Stem **īgland-**. Genitive singular **īglandes**; dative singular **īglande**; nominative plural **īgland**. This is the complete long-stem neuter model.

**męreswīn**, dolphin (neuter). Stem **męreswīn-**. Genitive singular **męreswīnes**; dative singular **męreswīne**; nominative plural **męreswīn**. Use every corresponding cell of **īgland**, replacing īgland- by the listed stem.
**weall**, wall (masculine). Stem **weall-**. Genitive singular **wealles**; dative singular **wealle**; nominative plural **weallas**. This is the complete ordinary consonant masculine model.
**geat**, gate (neuter). Stem **geat-**. Genitive singular **geates**; dative singular **geate**; nominative plural **gatu**.
**sumer**, summer (masculine). Stem **sumer-**. Genitive singular **sumeres**; dative singular **sumere**; nominative plural **sumeras**. Keep the medial e before each ending.

**winter**, winter (masculine). Stem **wintr-**. Genitive singular **wintres**; dative singular **wintre**; nominative plural **wintras**. The full form winter occurs in nominative and accusative singular; before endings use **wintr-**.

**lēad**, lead (metal) (neuter). Stem **lēad-**. Genitive singular **lēades**; dative singular **lēade**; nominative plural **lēad**. Use every corresponding cell of **īgland**, replacing īgland- by the listed stem. The plural is reference only.

**īsern**, iron (metal) (neuter). Stem **īsern-**. Genitive singular **īsernes**; dative singular **īserne**; nominative plural **īsern**. Use every corresponding cell of **īgland**, replacing īgland- by the listed stem. The plural is reference only. Keep its medial e before endings: the final syllable ends in rn.

**gimm**, gem; precious stone (masculine). Stem **gimm-**. Genitive singular **gimmes**; dative singular **gimme**; nominative plural **gimmas**. Use every corresponding cell of **weall**, replacing weall- by the listed stem.

**regn**, rain (masculine). Stem **regn-**. Genitive singular **regnes**; dative singular **regne**; nominative plural **regnas**. Use every corresponding cell of **weall**, replacing weall- by the listed stem. The plural is reference only. Cook also gives **rēn**; regn is the form selected for composition.

**torr**, tower (masculine). Stem **torr-**. Genitive singular **torres**; dative singular **torre**; nominative plural **torras**. Use every corresponding cell of **weall**, replacing weall- by the listed stem.

**seolh**, seal (masculine). Stem **sēol-**. Genitive singular **sēoles**; dative singular **sēole**; nominative plural **sēolas**. The bare nominative and accusative singular keep short eo and h. Before an ending, h disappears and the diphthong lengthens: **sēol-**.
**strǣt**, street (feminine). Stem **strǣt-**. Genitive singular **strǣte**; dative singular **strǣte**; nominative plural **strǣta**. This is the complete long-stem feminine model.

**mildheortnes**, mercy; mercies (feminine). Stem **mildheortness-**. Genitive singular **mildheortnesse**; dative singular **mildheortnesse**; nominative plural **mildheortnessa**. Use the endings of **strǣt** with **mildheortness-**, but keep the full headword **mildheortnes** in the endingless nominative singular. The final s is doubled before each ending. Both “mercy” and plural “mercies” are used here.

**frōfor**, comfort; consolation (feminine). Stem **frōfr-**. Genitive singular **frōfre**; dative singular **frōfre**; nominative plural **frōfra**. The nominative singular is the full **frōfor**; every ending-bearing cell uses **frōfr-**. Its plural is reference.

**sīðfæt**, journey; passage (masculine). Stem **sīðfæt-**. Genitive singular **sīðfætes**; dative singular **sīðfæte**; nominative plural **sīðfatas**. The singular uses sīðfæt- and the plural **sīðfat-**. This noun is masculine, so its nominative and accusative plural take -as.
**gebyrd**, birth (feminine). Stem **gebyrd-**. Genitive singular **gebyrde**; dative singular **gebyrde**; nominative plural **gebyrda**. Replace strǣt- by **gebyrd-** in every cell of strǣt.

**dēað**, death (masculine). Stem **dēað-**. Genitive singular **dēaðes**; dative singular **dēaðe**; nominative plural **dēaðas**. Use every corresponding cell of **weall**, replacing weall- by the listed stem. The plural is reference only.

**ceaster**, town; city (feminine). Stem **ceastr-**. Genitive singular **ceastre**; dative singular **ceastre**; nominative plural **ceastra**. Use **frōfor** as the full model: replace its ending-bearing stem frōfr- by **ceastr-**, and its full nominative singular frōfor by **ceaster**. Both numbers are available.

**bearn**, son; child (neuter). Stem **bearn-**. Genitive singular **bearnes**; dative singular **bearne**; nominative plural **bearn**. Use every corresponding cell of **īgland**, replacing īgland- by the listed stem. This ordinary “child; son” use does not alter the earlier capitalized title Bearn.

**fȳr**, fire (neuter). Stem **fȳr-**. Genitive singular **fȳres**; dative singular **fȳre**; nominative plural **fȳr**. Use every corresponding cell of **īgland**, replacing īgland- by the listed stem. The plural is reference only.

**mōna**, moon (masculine). Stem **mōn-**. Genitive singular **mōnan**; dative singular **mōnan**; nominative plural **mōnan**. The weak masculine differs from the weak feminine in nominative singular -a. Its astronomical singular is for composition; the plural is reference.

**sunne**, sun (feminine). Stem **sunn-**. Genitive singular **sunnan**; dative singular **sunnan**; nominative plural **sunnan**. Use every cell of **męregrēote**, replacing męregrēot- by **sunn-**. Thus nominative singular has sunn- + -e; the other singular cases have sunn- + -an. The astronomical singular is for composition; the plural is reference.

**seolfor**, silver (metal) (neuter). Stem **seolfr-**. Genitive singular **seolfres**; dative singular **seolfre**; nominative plural **seolfor**. Keep the full headword **seolfor** in all endingless nominative and accusative cells; use **seolfr-** before endings. The plural is reference.

**Hǣlend**, the Saviour; Jesus (proper title) (masculine). Stem **Hǣlend-**. Genitive singular **Hǣlendes**; dative singular **Hǣlende**. Use the singular cells of **weall**, replacing weall- by **Hǣlend-**. The four title forms are also given together below. There is no assigned proper-title plural.
**hāt**, hot. Stem **hāt-**. The long stem has no -u in strong feminine nominative singular or neuter nominative/accusative plural.

**blæc**, black. Stem **blæc-**. In the strong system, use **blac-** before a vowel ending, but retain **blæc-** before a consonantal ending or no ending. The short stem takes -u in strong feminine nominative singular and neuter nominative/accusative plural. The selected weak system uses **blac-** throughout.
**fæger**, beautiful; fair. Stem **fæger-**. The selected disyllabic model retains its internal e. Strong feminine nominative singular and neuter nominative/accusative plural have -u.

**rihtwīs**, righteous. Stem **rihtwīs-**. For every strong and weak cell, replace hāt- in the corresponding **hāt** table by the listed stem, retaining the ending or lack of ending. Instrumental reference limits remain the same.

**dēad**, dead. Stem **dēad-**. For every strong and weak cell, replace hāt- in the corresponding **hāt** table by the listed stem, retaining the ending or lack of ending. Instrumental reference limits remain the same.

**gesyndig**, favorable; fair (of winds). Stem **gesyndig-**. Replace fæger- by the listed stem in **every cell of both fæger tables**. Keep the internal vowel, including before -u, -re and -ra; the reference instrumentals follow the same operation.

**smylte**, calm; smooth. Stem **smylt-**. The endingless masculine and neuter singular use the full headword **smylte**. Elsewhere replace final -e by the required ending on **smylt-**. For example, feminine nominative singular has -u and dative plural -um.

**stille**, still; quiet. Stem **still-**. Use full **stille** in endingless masculine and neuter singular cells, and **still-** before endings. Simplify ll to l before consonantal -ne, -re and -ra: **stilne, stilre, stilra**. Retain ll before vowel endings: **stille, stilles, stillum**. The weak genitive plural is also stilra.

**ðurstig**, thirsty. Stem **ðurstig-**. Replace fæger- by the listed stem in **every cell of both fæger tables**. Keep the internal vowel, including before -u, -re and -ra; the reference instrumentals follow the same operation.
**dēorwierðra**, more precious. Stem **dēorwierðr-**. From dēorwierðe, remove final e and form the comparative stem **dēorwierðr-**. Comparatives remain weak even as predicates.

**fægerra**, more beautiful; fairer. Stem **fægerr-**. Use the entire **dēorwierðra** table, replacing comparative stem dēorwierðr- by **fægerr-** and keeping the same weak endings. Before genitive plural -ra, simplify the resulting consonant group to **fægerra**. The nominative singular is **fægerra, fægerre, fægerre**; the dative plural is **fægerrum** in all genders.

canonical_inflection_rule.description: All ordinary adjective NGDA cells are productive; distinct instrumental masculine/neuter singular cells remain recognition reference. Blæc changes æ to a before vowel endings; consonantal endings retain æ. The weak genitive plural likewise retains æ before the shared strong ending -ra: blæcra in every gender. Stille/smylte retain final e only where no ending replaces it. Stille simplifies ll before consonantal endings: stilne/stilre/stilra, but stille/stilles/stillum.
